text.p: Pakistan Telecommunications Company Ltd (PTCL) shares dropped 0.90 rupees, or 2.62 percent, to 33.35 on Sunday after its Global Depositary Receipt rates fell abroad, dealers said.
A turnover of 9.01 million shares of PTCL was recorded at the Karachi bourse in early trade.
"PTCL's five-year bond exchangeable into shares has had a negative impact," dealer Shakil Anwar said. "For foreigners the PTCL bond is now more attractive and they are unloading GDRs."

Dealer Ather Raouf said PTCL would remain weak in the near term. "The rate fixed for conversion of the PTCL bond into shares has limited the upside of the share price, which is negative for a liquid blue chip."

Last week's PTCL bond issue, led by Nomura International plc and Union Bank of Switzerland (East Asia) Ltd, was well received. The dollar-denominated bonds are convertible into fully paid "A" shares of PTCL held by the Pakistan government.
In 1994, the government floated 12 percent of PTCL's equity domestically in the form of common stocks and abroad as GDRs.
